findings.criterion: 12 ALTITUDE CONTRACT (typed projection from one read-only engine function) and 13 PORTFOLIO AT A GLANCE (from EXISTING portfolio index WITHOUT walking project roots)
findings.section: Wave 14 — Attention contract; Wave 15 — High Seat fold
findings.message: The draft asserts three incompatible storage facts at once: (a) Wave 14’s projection is ONE pure function that “performs zero writes”; (b) NS requires every project to PUBLISH a typed attention projection; (c) Wave 15 answers portfolio-at-a-glance and badge fold from the existing no-walk index with no root walk and High Seat write_authority none. If the function only reads the project ledger, the High Seat must visit N project stores to obtain N projections — that is a root walk, which criterion 13 forbids. If projections are already in the portfolio index, something must write them there on state change — that is a publish/write path the pure-function gate explicitly forbids and that Wave 14 never owns. “DERIVED ingest fires on a live write” (Wave 2 A5) is an audit observation, not a designed publish seam that Wave 14/15 bind to. Until the plan names the single legal path (who materializes projection rows into the index, on what event, with what read API that is not a root walk), criteria 12 and 13 cannot both be true, and the Wave-15 badge/glances tests are unfalsifiable plumbing theater.

findings.criterion: Wave-0 kill gate (“stage commissioned, executed by Anchor, validated handback”) and criterion 3 (nothing runs until confirm; commission is real spend)
findings.section: Wave 3 — BUILD-E / G4 substrate verdict
findings.message: Wave 3 treats G4 failure as an acceptable branch: “FAIL branch documented as direct-launch fallback with substrate integration named as its own follow-on scope.” Wave-0 and the product statement require Anchor to execute a confirmed commission and return a validated handback on a fresh project. A documented follow-on is not a pass. The draft never states that G4 FAIL is a plan HALT that blocks Waves 9–17, nor that the “direct-launch fallback” is in-scope, auth-ON tested, and dossier-joined the same way. As written, the executor wave can “done-when” with a FAIL verdict on file while later waves still claim end-to-end commission→handback. That is an unconfirmed-spend / fake-orchestration escape hatch against the kill gate.

findings.criterion: 6 (one campaign exercises AT LEAST TWO different commissioned skills) and Wave-0 full loop
findings.section: Wave 3 — BUILD-E; Wave 4 — step-type map; Wave 9 — Commission proposal; Wave 17 — Wave-0 kill gate
findings.message: Criterion 6 and Wave 17 require two different commissioned skills in one campaign. Wave 3 only proves “a real trio run” through job_runner/terminal_session/lanes for one confirmed commission shape. Wave 4’s step-type map names researchPrime, Crucible, Foreman, Gandalf, but Wave 3 never requires observed PID + returned handback for a second skill family. Non-goal forbids changing Crucible/Foreman/researchPrime internals; G5 may classify gates as REQUIRES-TRIO-CHANGE / INVISIBLE and exclude them from v1. The draft does not force Wave 17 to pick two skills that are both (a) executor-proven and (b) free of excluded HALTs. Skeptical default: the e2e will green on Foreman×2 or mock dispatch labels while researchPrime/Gandalf remain propose-only. That fails criterion 6 as written (“different commissioned skills”), not “two labels on one substrate path.”

findings.criterion: 4 (validated handback → REFLECTION RECEIPT + next-stage propose→confirm) and Wave-0
findings.section: Wave 4 — G5 HALT inventory; Wave 12 — Handback validation / reflection
findings.message: Wave 4 invents an exit: any commission path classed INVISIBLE or REQUIRES-TRIO-CHANGE is “excluded from v1 in the Face,” while non-goals forbid trio internal changes. Wave 12 and Wave-0 still require a validated handback that produces reflection + next-stage proposal. The plan never intersects these: there is no locked, test-enforced skill set for which handback is EXTERNALLY-OBSERVABLE end-to-end under auth ON, and no rule that Wave 17 may only commission that set. Without that intersection table as a machine-readable gate, “validated handback” can be satisfied by a fixture handback while live commissions sit parked at invisible human gates — exactly the silent non-orchestration the North Star forbids.

findings.criterion: 10 (roadmap_events has exactly ONE writer, proven by concurrency test)
findings.section: Wave 3 — BUILD-E; Wave 5 — Ledger spine; Wave 6 — Commission dossier
findings.message: Wave 3 launches real runs and records observed PID / handback before Wave 5 creates the single-writer spine and Wave 6’s dossier key. The draft does not forbid Wave 3 from writing roadmap/bind/launch records via the pre-spine paths (including the A4 non-atomic pair Wave 2 only documents). Criterion 10 is not “eventually one writer after Wave 5”; a second writer that remains reachable from the executor is a permanent dual path. Wave 5’s CI check can only police the tree as of Wave 5+; it does not automatically delete or quarantine Wave 3’s launch write sites. Order the spine (and dossier transaction) before any production commission write, or name Wave 3 as fixture-only with zero durable roadmap_events side effects — the draft does neither.

findings.criterion: 2 (one confirmed session ENVELOPE; exhaustion hard-stops; no per-sentence confirm)
findings.section: Wave 4 — compile-cost calibration; Wave 8 — Session envelope; Property gates — boundedness
findings.message: Criterion 2 and the confirmation-fatigue risk require a real envelope, not a slogan. Wave 4’s calibration “gates nothing,” yet Wave 8 “sizes from the Phase-1 calibration dataset as the default.” No numeric bound (dollars, tokens, compile count, reflection count) appears in the plan body; property-gate boundedness demands a named number plus a refusal path when exceeded. Exhaustion is described, but without a named unit and default, “hard stop” cannot be tested independently of whatever number an implementer invents. Calibration that gates nothing cannot authorize the envelope that authorizes all compiles and reflections — that is circular and unfalsifiable.

findings.criterion: 3 (confirm records who; nothing runs until confirm), 10 (one writer / no lost or duplicated ledger truth), risk of unconfirmed or double spend
findings.section: Wave 5–9, 12; Property gates — idempotence
findings.message: The hardening law in the draft states idempotence is real only if something re-invokes and asserts no change, and lists a repeat-invocation gate. Batch-confirm scaffolding, commission confirm, envelope confirm, and handback→reflection are all spend-adjacent identity events. No wave’s acceptance criteria require double-submit / re-delivery tests (second confirm does not launch a second run, does not mint a second job_id, does not emit a second reflection proposal). Without those, the concurrency hammer only proves append transport, not “exactly once” lifecycle identity. A skeptical reading: network retry or double-click creates two commissions or two reflections while every “one writer” test still passes.

findings.criterion: 9 (AUTH ON, asserted on outcomes), 12–13 (unknown never collapsed; unreadable → unknown row), 11 (honest-unknown)
findings.section: Wave 15–16 failure tables; Hardening-gate obligations — Failure-state table vocabulary
findings.message: The plan’s own emitted hardening law requires every surface-bearing wave to answer five dependency/backing states with status code AND user-visible text, and to keep unknown and empty as separate rows. Chamber UI and High Seat are the user-visible surfaces for criteria 7, 12, and 13. Their wave-local tables (loading / unreadable / unknown / empty; badge ambient containment) never map dependency-missing, dependency-slow-or-killed, dependency-returns-garbage, backing-store-unreadable, empty-but-valid. Portfolio index slow/killed/garbage is exactly how a “silently shorter list” or a false idle appears. Local named states without the required five-row surface table do not satisfy the plan’s own honesty gate, so “unknown never idle” remains prose.

findings.criterion: 1 (coarse steps + Oranges annotations), 4 (reflection with Oranges prompts), 5 (progressive elaboration from those annotations)
findings.section: Wave 7 — Scaffolding authoring; Wave 10 — Progressive elaboration; Wave 12 — Reflection receipt
findings.message: Waves 7/10/12 require Oranges annotation fields and prompts but never define a minimum content contract or a failing test for empty/boilerplate annotations. A compiler can emit `oranges: []` or stock placeholders, batch-confirm, and still pass “has Oranges fields.” Stage-start “targeted questions derived from Oranges” then degenerates to no-questions-derivable (a named state the plan already allows). That collapses progressive elaboration (criterion 5) and reflection foresight (criterion 4) into optional garnish while criterion 1 is green on schema shape. Skeptical-researcher bar: annotations must be non-empty, stage-specific, and sufficient to derive at least one elaboration question or an explicit offered researchPrime branch — proven by a negative test that rejects barren scaffolds.

findings.criterion: Statement (steward AUTHORS scaffolding; stage work COMMISSIONED — never authored by steward) and risk taxonomy (scaffolding mistaken for commissioned plan)
findings.section: Wave 7 — Scaffolding authoring; risk taxonomy “scaffolding mistaken for a commissioned plan”
findings.message: Wave 7 only stamps a provenance flag and asserts scaffolding is not routed through adversarial review. It does not require that commission/bind/executor paths REFUSE to treat a steward-authored scaffold step as if it were a commissioned plan artifact, nor that UI copy cannot present scaffold steps as “planned by Crucible/Foreman.” Labeling without a hard reject at the commission boundary fails the risk the North Star names. The mistaken-identity failure mode is enforcement, not metadata.

findings.criterion: 11 CONTINUITY (first message from ledger only; asks NO question whose answer is already recorded; dead run + missing handback NAMED)
findings.section: Wave 13 — Rehydration
findings.message: Wave 13 correctly bans model-invented facts and adds a no-re-ask guard, but never states that the first message is a pure deterministic render of ledger fields (template/composer with zero model calls). assembleBriefPacket is zero-model; the “first-message composer” is a separate deliverable with no such ban. A model can rephrase ledger truth into interrogatives the guard’s brittle string match misses, or omit naming the dead run / missing handback while still “proposing next step.” Criterion 11’s kill-everything-then-resume proof requires the wake-up path to be as model-free and field-complete as the brief packet join — the draft leaves a model-shaped hole exactly where continuity is claimed.

findings.criterion: 11 (dead mid-flight run and handback that never arrived — both NAMED, never silently absorbed); 8 (status reflects actual session state across park/restart/kill)
findings.section: Wave 11 — Session-state truth; Wave 12 — Handback; Wave 13 — Rehydration; Wave 17 — kill gate
findings.message: Naming anomalies is concentrated in Wave 13/17 scenarios. Wave 11 proves kill→dead status; Wave 12 names handback-missing as a failure state; neither requires that a run can be mid-flight dead AND a separate handback-never-arrived coexist as first-class dossier/status facts before rehydration. Criterion 11 demands both anomalies in one resume proof, not two alternate stories. Without a durable “expected handback not received” ledger fact distinct from “no commission yet” and “handback-invalid,” silent absorption remains possible: empty dossier fields read as idle/unknown and the wake-up test is fed a hand-built fixture the product loop never writes.

findings.criterion: 9–11 (outcome-asserted durability, continuity, single writer) and plan’s own law (“claim without matching obligation is a BLOCKER”)
findings.section: Property gates / Hardening-gate obligations
findings.message: The draft ends with durability/honesty/idempotence/boundedness/containment gates as unchecked boxes and repeated obligation lists, while waves claim atomic write, locks, concurrency, honest-unknown, and bounds. No wave done-when closes a specific checkbox; containment (escape-attempt for `..` / absolute / symlink) and idempotence (repeat-invocation) have no owning wave deliverable at all. Per the draft’s journal-0080 rule, a property claimed without a matching enforceable gate is a blocker-class plan defect. Leaving the emitted checklist empty while advertising hardening is exactly the “validating a rule is not providing it” failure the plan quotes.

findings.criterion: 13 failures. Audit-without-field-matrix is not consume-ready.
findings.section: Wave 15 — High Seat fold / portfolio at a glance
findings.message: Wave 15 says the glance is answered from engine/portfolio/query.mjs, but Wave 2’s A5 only audits liveness and DERIVED ingest — it does not prove the index already carries campaign stage, run liveness, and last movement at the grain criterion 13 requires. Non-goal forbids rebuilding the index; fix-items are allowed. The draft never requires the A5 coverage table to list, field-by-field, whether stage / live|waiting|blocked / last_movement are present today, and never schedules fix-items for each missing field before Wave 15. If those fields are absent, Wave 15 will either re-walk project roots (forbidden), invent a side cache (second source of truth), or show a thinner list — all

findings.criterion: 2 (envelope covers orchestrator-loop reflections) and 4 (on validated handback, emit reflection + propose next stage)
findings.section: Wave 8 — Session envelope; Wave 12 — unattended handback queue
findings.message: Gate Decision 1 queues unattended reflections with zero spend; Wave 12 then compiles + proposes at next session open, debiting the live envelope. Criterion 4’s happy path assumes a reflection receipt on validated handback; the draft does not specify whether “queued reflection” counts as having satisfied criterion 4’s emit, or only after session-open compile. If tests treat queue as success, overnight handbacks never produce the receipt artifact until John opens a session — acceptable for spend, but then criterion 4 must be restated as “queued or emitted.” If tests require immediate receipt, they contradict Decision 1. The plan leaves that contradiction unresolved.

findings.criterion: 3 tests reject fabricated display names. The draft allows the FAIL branch but does not require UI/outcome assertions that who is visibly non-identity. Skeptical residual: auth-ON green with a shared secret still looks like a named principal.
findings.section: Wave 4 — G6 identity resolution
findings.message: Recording `unattributed(shared_secret)` as who satisfies the field shape while collapsing multi-operator accountability to a shared credential class. Acceptable as an honest FAIL of subject recovery only if every spend UI and audit log renders that weakness permanently and

findings.section: Plan header / Success criteria
findings.message: The locked North Star is pasted in full twice, then restated again as bullet success criteria. Harmless to runtime truth but increases drift risk between copies; not a North Star criterion failure.

findings.criterion: 1 and 7 (“spoken description” / “spoken correction” as typed NL per glossary)
findings.section: Wave 4 Face glossary; Waves 7/16 “spoken”
findings.message: The plan correctly defines talking as typed NL and ASR out of scope, but still uses “spoken” in deliverables and done-whens. Low severity if tests accept typed NL; still a false-requirement trap for implementers who build ASR. Align vocabulary to “typed NL description/correction” everywhere criterion language is operationalized.

findings.criterion: Wave-0 kill gate; Success criteria 1–4 (spoken scaffolding → batch confirm → commission → handback → reflection + next-stage proposal)
findings.section: Waves 1–6 vs Wave 17 (Wave-0 kill gate)
findings.message: A competing product does not ship durability hammers, audit harnesses, and decision spikes for six waves before the user can describe a project and get a confirmed scaffold. This plan’s first *user-visible* scaffolding path is Wave 7; commission is Wave 9; the NS Wave-0 kill gate is Wave 17. Any thinner substitute (Claude/Cursor project chat + existing Ecgberht propose/confirm verbs the draft itself calls BUILT) already clears “talk → multi-stage plan → confirm spend” without this spine. If the competitive bar is the kill gate on a fresh project, burying it after optional substrate theater is a schedule shape that *guarantees* the effort loses the market-of-one (John) to tools he already has. The plan must force an early vertical slice that proves criteria 1–4 on auth ON *before* treating Waves 1–6 as a linear prerequisite wall, or admit the kill gate is not the true delivery order.

findings.criterion: Success criteria 3, 4, 6; Wave-0 kill gate (stage commissioned, executed by Anchor, validated handback)
findings.section: Wave 3 — BUILD-E / G4 substrate verdict
findings.message: Competitors that matter here (headless CLI agents, job runners, direct skill launch) already execute work after a human “go.” Wave 3 allows G4 FAIL to park real trio execution as “follow-on scope” with only a documented direct-launch fallback *outside* this effort. That is not a degraded mode of the North Star — it is a product exit. If Anchor cannot host a commissioned trio run, criteria 3–4–6 and Wave-0 are unsatisfiable *by this plan*, and John rationally stays on the competing path that already launches skills. The plan must bind a NS-satisfying FAIL path (executor still launches confirmed work through *some* Anchor-owned path with pid + handback + refusal-on-unconfirmed) as in-scope acceptance, not a polite abandonment note.

findings.criterion: 1 proof; glossary redefinition is not adjudication.
findings.section: Wave 4 — Face glossary; Wave 7 — dialogue → step_create
findings.message: The North Star’s first success criterion says **spoken**. The draft quietly rewrites that as “typed NL chat in the Anchor UI, ASR out of scope.” Voice-first competitors and plain phone-dictation-into-chat already meet “spoken → multi-stage plan” today. Shipping a typed-only compiler while still claiming criterion 1 is either (a) an unapproved North Star amendment smuggled into a glossary line, or (b) a competitive self-handicap that makes the steward strictly worse than “talk to any frontier chat.” Either amend the locked North Star explicitly or put a real speech→text path (even host-OS dictation acceptance tests) in the

findings.criterion: Success criterion 1 (PROPOSED multi-stage scaffolding with coarse steps + Oranges annotations)
findings.section: Wave 7 — Scaffolding authoring
findings.message: Wave 7’s acceptance proves *shape* (typed PROPOSAL, steward-authored flag, batch confirm, zero chat rows) and never proves *quality* against the free competitor John already uses: one message to a frontier model that returns a multi-stage plan with foresight annotations. If steward-authored scaffolds are coarser, wronger, or Oranges-weaker than that free turn, the batch-confirm ceremony is pure tax and the product loses on the same criterion it claims. The plan needs an adversarial quality gate (fixture intents; minimum stage count; Oranges fields non-empty and stage-specific; human-or-judge rubric that free-chat baseline does not dominate) — structure-only green is a competitive paper win.

findings.criterion: Success criteria 2, 3, 6; Risk taxonomy CONFIRMATION FATIGUE; Statement “driven OVER TIME”
findings.section: Waves 8–9 — Session envelope; Commission proposal
findings.message: Competitors (Cursor agent, Claude Code, Devin-class loops) take one session trust boundary and then *work*. This plan’s envelope covers compiles/reflections but **explicitly not commissions**; criterion 6 forces ≥2 skills ⇒ ≥2 full propose→confirm→who ceremonies on top of scaffold batch-confirm and envelope confirm. That is more gatekeeping than the competing agent UIs John will compare against, and it re-opens the confirmation-fatigue risk the envelope was invented to kill. Either the envelope (or a campaign-level spend envelope) must cover a bounded set of pre-declared commission *classes* with per-spend *showing* still required, or the plan must prove with a fatigue budget that multi-skill campaigns stay under a named confirm count. As written, the product loses the “lightweight over time” race to tools that confirm once and run.

findings.criterion: 4 reflection + next-stage proposal until John opens a session. That is a competitive continuity hole: portfolio says “ready,” campaign brain says “asleep.” The North Star wants spend gated, not *thinking* gated. At minimum, unattended path must produce ledger-native REFLECTION RECEIPT + next-stage PROPOSAL artifacts without model spend (template/deterministic compile) or the plan must prove why “driven OVER TIME” still wins when every stage boundary waits for a morning session.
findings.section: Wave 12 — unattended handback queue; Gate Decision 1
findings.message: Overnight-agent competitors progress while the human sleeps: handback lands, next step is proposed, badge or push fires. This plan’s gate decision *queues* reflection and refuses next-stage proposal compile until session open — zero unattended spend, but also zero unattended *orchestration*. High Seat may show `deliverable_ready` (Wave 14–15) while the steward still has not emitted the

findings.criterion: facing claims about “live/waiting/blocked runs” (plural) to honest singular capacity; if not, Wave 3 must treat concurrent run capacity as required for Wave-0/17, not a footnote in a gate report. Shipping serial orchestration into a portfolio High Seat built for N projects is a competitive regression versus tools that already parallelize.
findings.section: Wave 3 — BUILD-E (one-run-at-a-time DEGRADED); Wave 17 gate report
findings.message: Multi-agent competitors run parallel workstreams. Declaring one-run-at-a-time as acceptable DEGRADED v1 means a campaign that must exercise two skills (criterion 6) is forced serial, portfolio-at-a-glance never stress-tests concurrent live runs, and continuity (criterion 11) under dual live/dead mixtures is under-proven. If DEGRADED is permanent, the plan should change

findings.criterion: Success criterion 7 (stage artifacts render reviewably; spoken correction → new version)
findings.section: Wave 16 — Chamber UI; earlier waves’ artifact claims
findings.message: Competing products render plans and diffs the moment work returns. This plan can green Waves 1–15 (including handbacks, reflections, and deliverable_ready) while criterion 7’s *human* surface — chamber steps/proposals/artifacts/corrections — still does not exist until Wave 16. That is a competitive dead product for most of the build: ledger truth without reviewable UI is a backend demo, not “artifacts render reviewably.” Pull a minimal review surface (even read-only artifact card + confirm affordance) into the first wave that emits stage artifacts (≤ Wave 12), or criterion 7 remains an end-loaded fiction competitors already satisfy with a markdown pane.

findings.criterion: Success criterion 3 (confirmation records `who`); Success criterion 9 (AUTH ON, outcomes)
findings.section: Wave 4 — G6 identity resolution
findings.message: Competitors with real auth (GitHub, Google, workspace SSO) record an accountable principal. Wave 4’s FAIL path writes `who = unattributed(shared_secret)` and still claims criterion 3. That is ceremony without accountability: AUTH ON green tests can pass while every spend is attributed to a blob no human can audit. A competing internal tool that logs the OS user or token subject beats this on the same criterion. Either G6 PASS (recoverable subject) is a hard gate for spend confirmation, or the North Star’s `who` must be rewritten; “honest unattributed” is competitor-losing honesty theater.

findings.criterion: Success criteria 8, 11 (roadmap/session truth across kill/restart; continuity names true state; never silently absorbed)
findings.section: Wave 4 — G5 HALT inventory
findings.message: Competitors that own the full agent loop either auto-continue, surface the gate, or fail the job visibly. This plan classifies INVISIBLE HALTs and *excludes them from v1* while still claiming commissions are “executed by Anchor” with honest live/dead/waiting status. A confirmed Foreman/Crucible run stuck on an invisible human gate will look `working` or lease-live until TTL magic, then become a continuity lie — exactly the status-drift risk the taxonomy names — and John will trust Cursor’s visible waits more than Anchor’s silent ones. v1 must either (a) refuse to commission paths with INVISIBLE HALTs, (b) externalize them as named `needs_you` with ledger events, or (c) drop those skills from the dispatch map. Excluding the failure mode from the Face is not competitive reliability.

findings.criterion: Success criterion 2 (one confirmed session ENVELOPE; exhaustion hard-stops)
findings.section: Wave 4 — compile-cost measurement; Wave 8 — envelope default
findings.message: Competing agent UIs either show live cost and soft-extend, or they don’t pretend to budget. Wave 4 gathers ≥20-compile calibration then says it “gates nothing,” while Wave 8 sizes the default envelope from that dataset. A wrong default plus hard-stop mid-authoring is worse UX than competitors with no envelope at all: John hits `envelope-exhausted` during the “lightweight” path and re-confirms, reintroducing per-burst friction criterion 2 forbids. Calibration must gate the default (median/p90 → named budget with UI preview before confirm) or exhaustion tests will pass while real sessions thrash — a competitive own-goal on the lightweight claim.

findings.criterion: Success criteria 3, 5, 6 (commission shows skill+seat+depth; progressive elaboration may offer researchPrime; ≥2 skills in one campaign)
findings.section: Wave 4 — step-type map; Wave 9 — dispatch
findings.message: Flexible competitors let the human pick the tool for the stage. This plan hard-binds RESEARCH→researchPrime, PLAN→Crucible, BUILD→Foreman, REVIEW→Gandalf and only tests collision refusal. Progressive elaboration (criterion 5) can offer researchPrime, but a research-shaped stage that should be Gandalf (or a build-shaped spike that should not yet be Foreman) cannot be commissioned without fighting the map. That rigidity loses to “same steward, pick skill” products and risks criterion 6 becoming two *forced* skills rather than two *useful* ones. The map needs an override path (still propose→confirm with skill visible) or staged multi-map versions; locked four-bin dispatch is competitor-brittle.

findings.criterion: Success criterion 11 (CONTINUITY — first message states where the campaign is from ledger only; proposes next step with why; no re-ask)
findings.section: Wave 13 — Rehydration
findings.message: The competing continuity product is brutal and free: reopen the chat thread. Wave 13 tests no-re-ask, named dead run, named missing handback, honest-unknown — necessary but not sufficient. It never proves the wake-up message is *as useful as* scrolling the competitor transcript (ordering, why, options, waiting-on-John salience). If ledger rehydration is a colder, shorter, more bureaucratic brief than “read last Claude Project,” John will keep the chat competitor as system of record and treat the steward as optional chrome — criterion 11 fails in practice while tests stay green. Add a competitive usefulness gate: same fixture, wake-up must include stage, anomalies, waiting decisions, next step + why, and must not be information-worse than a fixed chat-baseline transcript fixture.

findings.criterion: Success criteria 12, 13 (altitude contract; portfolio at a glance from existing index)
findings.section: Wave 15 vs Wave 17 kill gate
findings.message: Competitors for “portfolio at a glance” are Linear, GitHub Projects, and the already-built High Seat/index — multi-project by default. Wave 17’s kill gate is a **single** fresh-project campaign. Waves 12–14 can pass in isolation while Wave 15’s multi-project unknown-row and one-poll badge proofs never ride the same auth-ON outcome suite as the campaign story. That is how you ship a steward that wins one-project demos and loses the High Seat competitor the North Star named. Fold a multi-project leg into the Wave-0/17 proof: ≥2 active projects, one unreadable → `unknown` row (list length preserved), one `needs_you` → badge within one poll, zero extra ambient — or criteria 12–13 remain side quests.

findings.criterion: Prior art “MUST build on”; Non-goal “Do not re-plan or rebuild the portfolio tracking index”; Wave-0 kill gate
findings.section: Success criteria BUILD-vs-WIRE; Waves 1–6; Non-goal portfolio index
findings.message: The competitive alternative inside the same monorepo is: wire BUILT Ecgberht propose/confirm/bind, packet-view, receipt-validate, brief, high-seat, portfolio query — and only build the verified-absent Anchor executor + dialogue→scaffold + attention emitters. This plan instead fronts a new durability law, spine, dossier, and audit empire before wiring. That invites a second ledger/spine culture the risk taxonomy fears and slows the only race that matters (Wave-0). A competitor team doing “adapter-first” ships the kill gate while this plan is still proving removal-proof locks. Reorder so every early wave is either (a) a named fix against BUILT seams (A3/A4/A5) or (b) the missing Anchor half — not a parallel storage religion that re-derives what prior art already paid for.

findings.criterion: Success criteria 4 and 12 (reflection + next-stage propose→confirm; `deliverable_ready` altitude)
findings.message: Attention competitors (Slack, email digests, Linear notifications) couple “something finished” to “here is the decision.” This plan can emit bundle-hash-gated `deliverable_ready` into the badge while the next-stage PROPOSAL is still queued behind a live envelope (unattended path). John opens High Seat, sees ready, drills in, and finds no confirmable next step — worse than a competitor that only notifies when an action exists. Define altitude so `deliverable_ready` requires a ledger-visible next action (proposal or explicit “reflection queued — open session to compile”) or split states so the badge never claims readiness the steward cannot act on. Otherwise criteria 4 and 12 race each other and the High Seat loses trust to dumber, consistent notifiers.

findings.criterion: Success criterion 7 (spoken correction → new version through propose→confirm)
findings.section: Wave 4 — amendment-vs-recommission decision “recorded in the Face”
findings.message: Competing PM tools make “edit this artifact” vs “spawn new work” obvious. Parking the amendment-vs-recommission rule as a Face prose line without Wave 16 acceptance tests lets the chamber ship a correction path that either always recommissions (expensive vs competitors’ inline edit) or always amends (silent scope creep). Promote it to a machine-readable decision the correction path imports, with tests for both branches.

findings.criterion: Success criterion 3 (skill + seat + depth shown before spend)
findings.section: Wave 9 — proposal renders estimated spend
findings.message: Competitors that show cost either meter for real or omit the number. Wave 9 requires “estimated spend” on the proposal with no honesty bar (source of estimate, wrong-estimate failure state, or link to Wave 4 calibration). A confident wrong dollar amount is worse than competitors showing nothing — it trains John to ignore the confirm surface. Tie estimates to the calibration record or label them `unknown` as a first-class proposal field.

findings.criterion: Wave-0 kill gate — spoken description → proposed scaffolding → batch confirm → stage commissioned → validated handback → REFLECTION + NEXT-STAGE PROPOSAL, auth ON; kill-everything reopen names true state; also criteria 1, 4, 11
findings.section: Wave 17 — Wave-0 kill gate; wave sequence overall
findings.message: The North Star’s Wave-0 kill gate is the product definition of done, not a nice-to-have capstone. This plan puts the only end-to-end proof in Wave 17 of 17. Waves 1–16 can go fully green while the kill gate remains unrun. A bored investor does not fund sixteen substrate and partial-loop waves on the promise that the campaign loop will “eventually” close. Either insert an early vertical-slice acceptance (minimum: describe → batch-confirm scaffolding → one confirmed commission → handback → reflection+next-stage proposal + a kill-resume leg) with a hard HALT if it fails, or admit the plan has no early kill and re-cut scope until it does. “Criteria traceability report” at the end is not a substitute for an early kill.

findings.criterion: 3 (commission proposed, nothing runs until confirm, then real spend path); Wave-0 kill gate (stage commissioned, executed by Anchor, validated handback); statement “Stage work is COMMISSIONED … never authored by the steward”
findings.section: Wave 3 — BUILD-E — the Anchor commission executor and the G4 substrate verdict
findings.message: Wave 3 settles G4 with PASS = observed pid + returned handback, and on FAIL merely “documents … direct-launch fallback … follow-on scope.” That is not a plan gate; it is a hope. The plan still chains Waves 9, 12, and 17 onto “real trio” execution as if G4 were assumed true. Refute: G4 FAIL must be an explicit plan HALT or mandatory re-scope (what ships without live commission execution, what is cut from Wave-0) before any later wave spends capital. “Named as follow-on” after building fourteen more waves is how science projects eat the budget and never ship the kill gate.

findings.criterion: 1 (batch-confirmed scaffolding); 3 (skill+seat+depth shown before spend); 7 (stage artifacts render reviewably; spoken correction → new version through propose→confirm); statement “typed ledger artifacts rendered into conversation”

A bored investor treats a loop that is only true in tests and CLI as unsellable. Criterion 2’s lightweight authoring and the fatigue risk both depend on a credible bound. “Gates nothing” is investor-speak for “optional science.” Make the calibration record a hard input to the envelope default (with a documented fallback constant if measurement fails) or cut it from the critical path.

findings.topic: envelope bound unnamed and calibration ungated

findings.criterion: 2 (one confirmed session ENVELOPE; exhaustion hard-stops; no per-sentence confirm)

Batch-confirm scaffolding, commission confirm, envelope confirm, and handback→reflection are all spend-adjacent identity events. findings.topic: product loop deferred behind six substrate waves
findings.section: Waves 1–6 vs Wave 17 (Wave-0 kill gate)
findings.criterion: Wave-0 kill gate; Success criteria 1–4 (spoken scaffolding → batch confirm → commission → handback → reflection + next-stage proposal)
findings.message: A competing product does not ship durability hammers, audit harnesses, and decision spikes for six waves before the user can describe a project and get a confirmed scaffold. High Seat may show `deliverable_ready` (Wave 14–15) while the steward still has not emitted the

findings.section: Wave 3 — BUILD-E (one-run-at-a-time DEGRADED); Wave 17 gate report
findings.criterion: facing claims about “live/waiting/blocked runs” (plural) to honest singular capacity; if not, Wave 3 must treat concurrent run capacity as required for Wave-0/17, not a footnote in a gate report. Shipping serial orchestration into a portfolio High Seat built for N projects is a competitive regression versus tools that already parallelize.
findings.message: Multi-agent competitors run parallel workstreams. Declaring one-run-at-a-time as acceptable DEGRADED v1 means a campaign that must exercise two skills (criterion 6) is forced serial, portfolio-at-a-glance never stress-tests concurrent live runs, and continuity (criterion 11) under dual live/dead mixtures is under-proven. If DEGRADED is permanent, the plan should change

findings.section: Wave 16 — Chamber UI; earlier waves’ artifact claims
findings.criterion: Success criterion 7 (stage artifacts render reviewably; spoken correction → new version)
findings.message: Competing products render plans and diffs the moment work returns. This plan can green Waves 1–15 (including handbacks, reflections, and deliverable_ready) while criterion 7’s *human* surface — chamber steps/proposals/artifacts/corrections — still does not exist until Wave 16. That is a competitive dead product for most of the build: ledger truth without reviewable UI is a backend demo, not “artifacts render reviewably.” Pull a minimal review surface (even read-only artifact card + confirm affordance) into the first wave that emits stage artifacts (≤ Wave 12), or criterion 7 remains an end-loaded fiction competitors already satisfy with a markdown pane.

findings.topic: who reduced to unattributed shared secret
findings.section: Wave 4 — G6 identity resolution
findings.criterion: Success criterion 3 (confirmation records `who`); Success criterion 9 (AUTH ON, outcomes)
findings.message: Competitors with real auth (GitHub, Google, workspace SSO) record an accountable principal. Wave 4’s FAIL path writes `who = unattributed(shared_secret)` and still claims criterion 3. That is ceremony without accountability: AUTH ON green tests can pass while every spend is attributed to a blob no human can audit. A competing internal tool that logs the OS user or token subject beats this on the same criterion. Either G6 PASS (recoverable subject) is a hard gate for spend confirmation, or the North Star’s `who` must be rewritten; “honest unattributed” is competitor-losing honesty theater.

findings.topic: invisible trio HALTs excluded from v1
findings.section: Wave 4 — G5 HALT inventory
findings.criterion: Success criteria 8, 11 (roadmap/session truth across kill/restart; continuity names true state; never silently absorbed)
findings.message: Competitors that own the full agent loop either auto-continue, surface the gate, or fail the job visibly. This plan classifies INVISIBLE HALTs and *excludes them from v1* while still claiming commissions are “executed by Anchor” with honest live/dead/waiting status. A confirmed Foreman/Crucible run stuck on an invisible human gate will look `working` or lease-live until TTL magic, then become a continuity lie — exactly the status-drift risk the taxonomy names — and John will trust Cursor’s visible waits more than Anchor’s silent ones. v1 must either (a) refuse to commission paths with INVISIBLE HALTs, (b) externalize them as named `needs_you` with ledger events, or (c) drop those skills from the dispatch map. Excluding the failure mode from the Face is not competitive reliability.

findings.section: Wave 4 — compile-cost measurement; Wave 8 — envelope default
findings.criterion: Success criterion 2 (one confirmed session ENVELOPE; exhaustion hard-stops)
findings.message: Competing agent UIs either show live cost and soft-extend, or they don’t pretend to budget. Wave 4 gathers ≥20-compile calibration then says it “gates nothing,” while Wave 8 sizes the default envelope from that dataset. A wrong default plus hard-stop mid-authoring is worse UX than competitors with no envelope at all: John hits `envelope-exhausted` during the “lightweight” path and re-confirms, reintroducing per-burst friction criterion 2 forbids. Calibration must gate the default (median/p90 → named budget with UI preview before confirm) or exhaustion tests will pass while real sessions thrash — a competitive own-goal on the lightweight claim.

findings.section: Wave 4 — step-type map; Wave 9 — dispatch
findings.criterion: Success criteria 3, 5, 6 (commission shows skill+seat+depth; progressive elaboration may offer researchPrime; ≥2 skills in one campaign)
findings.message: Flexible competitors let the human pick the tool for the stage. This plan hard-binds RESEARCH→researchPrime, PLAN→Crucible, BUILD→Foreman, REVIEW→Gandalf and only tests collision refusal. Progressive elaboration (criterion 5) can offer researchPrime, but a research-shaped stage that should be Gandalf (or a build-shaped spike that should not yet be Foreman) cannot be commissioned without fighting the map. That rigidity loses to “same steward, pick skill” products and risks criterion 6 becoming two *forced* skills rather than two *useful* ones. The map needs an override path (still propose→confirm with skill visible) or staged multi-map versions; locked four-bin dispatch is competitor-brittle.

findings.section: Wave 13 — Rehydration
findings.criterion: Success criterion 11 (CONTINUITY — first message states where the campaign is from ledger only; proposes next step with why; no re-ask)
findings.message: The competing continuity product is brutal and free: reopen the chat thread. Wave 13 tests no-re-ask, named dead run, named missing handback, honest-unknown — necessary but not sufficient. It never proves the wake-up message is *as useful as* scrolling the competitor transcript (ordering, why, options, waiting-on-John salience). If ledger rehydration is a colder, shorter, more bureaucratic brief than “read last Claude Project,” John will keep the chat competitor as system of record and treat the steward as optional chrome — criterion 11 fails in practice while tests stay green. Add a competitive usefulness gate: same fixture, wake-up must include stage, anomalies, waiting decisions, next step + why, and must not be information-worse than a fixed chat-baseline transcript fixture.

findings.topic: portfolio criteria not in Wave-0 e2e
findings.section: Wave 15 vs Wave 17 kill gate
findings.criterion: Success criteria 12, 13 (altitude contract; portfolio at a glance from existing index)
findings.message: Competitors for “portfolio at a glance” are Linear, GitHub Projects, and the already-built High Seat/index — multi-project by default. Wave 17’s kill gate is a **single** fresh-project campaign. Waves 12–14 can pass in isolation while Wave 15’s multi-project unknown-row and one-poll badge proofs never ride the same auth-ON outcome suite as the campaign story. That is how you ship a steward that wins one-project demos and loses the High Seat competitor the North Star named. Fold a multi-project leg into the Wave-0/17 proof: ≥2 active projects, one unreadable → `unknown` row (list length preserved), one `needs_you` → badge within one poll, zero extra ambient — or criteria 12–13 remain side quests.

findings.section: Success criteria BUILD-vs-WIRE; Waves 1–6; Non-goal portfolio index
findings.criterion: Prior art “MUST build on”; Non-goal “Do not re-plan or rebuild the portfolio tracking index”; Wave-0 kill gate
findings.message: The competitive alternative inside the same monorepo is: wire BUILT Ecgberht propose/confirm/bind, packet-view, receipt-validate, brief, high-seat, portfolio query — and only build the verified-absent Anchor executor + dialogue→scaffold + attention emitters. This plan instead fronts a new durability law, spine, dossier, and audit empire before wiring. That invites a second ledger/spine culture the risk taxonomy fears and slows the only race that matters (Wave-0). A competitor team doing “adapter-first” ships the kill gate while this plan is still proving removal-proof locks. Reorder so every early wave is either (a) a named fix against BUILT seams (A3/A4/A5) or (b) the missing Anchor half — not a parallel storage religion that re-derives what prior art already paid for.

findings.criterion: Success criteria 4 and 12 (reflection + next-stage propose→confirm; `deliverable_ready` altitude)
findings.message: Attention competitors (Slack, email digests, Linear notifications) couple “something finished” to “here is the decision.” This plan can emit bundle-hash-gated `deliverable_ready` into the badge while the next-stage PROPOSAL is still queued behind a live envelope (unattended path). John opens High Seat, sees ready, drills in, and finds no confirmable next step — worse than a competitor that only notifies when an action exists. Define altitude so `deliverable_ready` requires a ledger-visible next action (proposal or explicit “reflection queued — open session to compile”) or split states so the badge never claims readiness the steward cannot act on. Otherwise criteria 4 and 12 race each other and the High Seat loses trust to dumber, consistent notifiers.

findings.section: Wave 4 — amendment-vs-recommission decision “recorded in the Face”
findings.criterion: Success criterion 7 (spoken correction → new version through propose→confirm)
findings.message: Competing PM tools make “edit this artifact” vs “spawn new work” obvious. Parking the amendment-vs-recommission rule as a Face prose line without Wave 16 acceptance tests lets the chamber ship a correction path that either always recommissions (expensive vs competitors’ inline edit) or always amends (silent scope creep). Promote it to a machine-readable decision the correction path imports, with tests for both branches.

findings.section: Wave 9 — proposal renders estimated spend
findings.criterion: Success criterion 3 (skill + seat + depth shown before spend)
findings.message: Competitors that show cost either meter for real or omit the number. Wave 9 requires “estimated spend” on the proposal with no honesty bar (source of estimate, wrong-estimate failure state, or link to Wave 4 calibration). A confident wrong dollar amount is worse than competitors showing nothing — it trains John to ignore the confirm surface. Tie estimates to the calibration record or label them `unknown` as a first-class proposal field.

reviews.note: Analyst Shark · bored-investor angle. Refutations only; inclusion-tested against NS v4. Severity is capital-at-risk / time-to-kill-gate, not prose taste.

findings.section: Wave 17 — Wave-0 kill gate; wave sequence overall
findings.criterion: Wave-0 kill gate — spoken description → proposed scaffolding → batch confirm → stage commissioned → validated handback → REFLECTION + NEXT-STAGE PROPOSAL, auth ON; kill-everything reopen names true state; also criteria 1, 4, 11
findings.message: The North Star’s Wave-0 kill gate is the product definition of done, not a nice-to-have capstone. This plan puts the only end-to-end proof in Wave 17 of 17. Waves 1–16 can go fully green while the kill gate remains unrun. A bored investor does not fund sixteen substrate and partial-loop waves on the promise that the campaign loop will “eventually” close. Either insert an early vertical-slice acceptance (minimum: describe → batch-confirm scaffolding → one confirmed commission → handback → reflection+next-stage proposal + a kill-resume leg) with a hard HALT if it fails, or admit the plan has no early kill and re-cut scope until it does. “Criteria traceability report” at the end is not a substitute for an early kill.

findings.section: Wave 3 — BUILD-E — the Anchor commission executor and the G4 substrate verdict
findings.criterion: 3 (commission proposed, nothing runs until confirm, then real spend path); Wave-0 kill gate (stage commissioned, executed by Anchor, validated handback); statement “Stage work is COMMISSIONED … never authored by the steward”
findings.message: Wave 3 settles G4 with PASS = observed pid + returned handback, and on FAIL merely “documents … direct-launch fallback … follow-on scope.” That is not a plan gate; it is a hope. If the substrate cannot host a commissioned trio run under the steward, criteria 3, 4, 6 and the Wave-0 path that require execution and validated handback are not deliverable inside this effort. The plan still chains Waves 9, 12, and 17 onto “real trio” execution as if G4 were assumed true. Refute: G4 FAIL must be an explicit plan HALT or mandatory re-scope (what ships without live commission execution, what is cut from Wave-0) before any later wave spends capital. “Named as follow-on” after building fourteen more waves is how science projects eat the budget and never ship the kill gate.

findings.section: Wave 16 — Chamber UI; Waves 7–12 confirm/propose paths
findings.criterion: 1 (batch-confirmed scaffolding); 3 (skill+seat+depth shown before spend); 7 (stage artifacts render reviewably; spoken correction → new version through propose→confirm); statement “typed ledger artifacts rendered into conversation”
findings.message: Human-facing steps, proposal/confirm surfaces, and artifact cards land in Wave 16 — after the authoring, envelope, commission, elaboration, session-state, handback/reflection, rehydration, attention, and High Seat waves. Earlier waves can assert engine verbs and typed events while John still has no reviewable chamber path for the confirmations and artifacts the North Star requires him to see. Criterion 7 is not “packet-view exists in Ecgberht”; it is stage artifacts render reviewably and corrections produce versions through propose→confirm on a surface he uses. A bored investor treats a loop that is only true in tests and CLI as unsellable. Either pull a minimal confirm + artifact surface forward to the first vertical slice, or stop claiming criteria 1/3/7 are met by mid-plan wave greens.

findings.section: Wave 4 — Decision records and spikes (compile-cost measurement); Wave 8 — Session envelope
findings.criterion: 2 (one confirmed session ENVELOPE covers compiles AND orchestrator-loop reflections; exhaustion hard-stops); risk taxonomy CONFIRMATION FATIGUE (envelope must cover reflections)
findings.message: Wave 4 spends real work on “≥20 real compiles … emitted as a machine-readable calibration record; gates nothing.” Wave 8 then sizes the default envelope “from the Phase-1 calibration dataset.” That is a contradiction with capital: either calibration is the authority for the default budget and Wave 4 is not done-when-green without a usable default (and a named numeric bound), or Wave 8 invents a default and the ≥20-compile exercise is dead weight. Criterion 2’s lightweight authoring and the fatigue risk both depend on a credible bound. “Gates nothing” is investor-speak for “optional science.” Make the calibration record a hard input to the envelope default (with a documented fallback constant if measurement fails) or cut it from the critical path.

findings.section: Wave 17 — Wave-0 kill gate; Wave 9 — Commission proposal (dispatch map)
findings.criterion: 6 (one campaign exercises AT LEAST TWO different commissioned skills)
findings.message: Criterion 6 is only asserted in the final campaign test. Waves 3, 9, and 12 can green on a single skill path (e.g. only Foreman or only researchPrime). The step-type map in Wave 4 is a decision record, not a multi-skill exercise. A bored investor assumes the second skill path will fail late (seat wiring, handback shape, G5 HALT profile differences) after the budget is spent. Require an intermediate multi-skill obligation (two distinct commissioned skills through propose→confirm→handback, or at least propose→confirm with executor smoke for two skills) before the High Seat / chamber waves, not only inside Wave 17.

findings.section: Waves 1–6 vs Wave 7 — Scaffolding authoring
findings.criterion: 1 (spoken description → PROPOSED multi-stage scaffolding, batch-confirmed; zero chat turns persisted)
findings.message: Criterion 1 is the first success criterion and the first half of Wave-0. This plan does not open a dialogue→step_create path until Wave 7, after durability hammer, four audit harnesses, commission executor, spikes/decisions, single-writer spine, and commission dossier. Substrate is real risk — but six full waves with zero progress on “spoken description → proposed scaffolding” is a portfolio bet that ground truth must be perfect before the product exists. Bored-investor cut: collapse or parallelize audits/spikes that do not block a thin scaffolding slice; prove criterion 1 on a fixture ledger early; keep durability/spine as hard gates for write paths without making them a six-wave wall before any authoring demo.

findings.section: Property gates / Hardening-gate obligations; Waves 1, 5, 8 (and plan-wide claims)
findings.criterion: 10 (`roadmap_events` exactly ONE writer, proven by concurrency test); 2 (bounded session envelope with exhaustion hard-stop); 9 (asserted on outcomes rather than plumbing)
findings.message: The plan ends by declaring durability, honesty, idempotence, boundedness, and containment “asserted by this plan,” with the plan’s own law that a named property without a matching mechanical gate is a BLOCKER. Waves clearly own durability (atomic write, lock, concurrency, removal-proof) and many honesty failure tables. They do not clearly own: (a) named numeric bounds + refusal for envelope and event/store reads, (b) repeat-invocation / exactly-once tests beyond “concurrency,” (c) escape-attempt containment tests for project-relative stores. Unchecked gate checklists at the bottom are not obligations assigned to waves. Either map each asserted property to a wave deliverable + done-when test, or stop claiming the property. Investor read of empty checkboxes next to “asserted by this plan” is fake assurance.

findings.section: Wave 2 — A1/A2/A4/A5 audit harnesses and the fix-item ledger; Wave 15 — High Seat fold
findings.criterion: 13 (PORTFOLIO AT A GLANCE from EXISTING portfolio index; unreadable → unknown); non-goal “Do not re-plan or rebuild the portfolio tracking index”
findings.message: Wave 2 is allowed to discover an open-ended set of A5 gaps, schedule each as a fix-item on “owning waves,” and Wave 15 cannot complete until “all A5 fix items [are] closed.” That is an uncapped scope injector on the critical path to criterion 13. Audits are correct; unbounded repair absorbed into feature waves is how “consume the index” becomes a stealth rebuild. Cap it: severity tiers, max fix-items in-scope for this plan, explicit defer/out-of-scope for the rest, and a rule that A5 defects beyond the cap are named DEGRADED on the Wave-0 report rather than infinite work before portfolio-at-a-glance.

findings.section: Wave dependencies (esp. Wave 4 depends on Wave 3; Wave 2 on Wave 1)
findings.criterion: Wave-0 kill gate (time-to-proof of the full campaign loop); criteria 1–4 as first user-visible value
findings.message: Wave 4 (G2 render, G3 handback validate, G5 HALT inventory, G6 identity, step-type map, compile calibration) depends on Wave 3 (Anchor executor + G4). Most of those spikes need real fixtures and existing Ecgberht modules, not a live job_runner commission path. Serializing them behind BUILD-E lengthens calendar time to every later wave for no product reason. Same pattern: full target-box durability hammer as a hard prefix before audits that are mostly read-only probes. Bored investor scores plans on critical-path length to the first killable demo. Parallelize independent spikes/audits; reserve true serial edges for write-spine → dossier → authoring → commission → handback.

findings.section: Wave 3 — one-run-at-a-time DEGRADED mode; Wave 17 — Gate report listing DEGRADED
findings.criterion: 8 (roadmap status reflects ACTUAL session state across park, restart, kill); 11 (first message states live/dead/waiting runs — plural realism)
findings.message: Declaring one-run-at-a-time as the DEGRADED mode is honest; leaving no promotion criterion or test pressure for multi-run/waiting coexistence makes degraded the permanent product. Criteria 8 and 11 speak in plurals (runs, waiting, blocked). Wave 17 “list DEGRADED by name” is labeling, not a path off the island. Specify whether multi-run is in-scope for this plan’s kill gate or explicitly out with a named follow-on; if in-scope, add at least one test with two run records in distinct states (live + dead, or waiting + blocked) so status/rehydration cannot green on a single-run toy.

findings.section: Wave 17 vs Waves 1–16 acceptance style
findings.criterion: 9 (all of it passes with AUTH ON, asserted on outcomes rather than plumbing)
findings.message: Criterion 9 demands auth ON and outcome-level assertion, not plumbing. The plan correctly flips auth ON in Wave 1, then spends many wave gates on CI diff fences, invariant checks, and harness tables — necessary substrate, but not “outcomes.” Only Wave 17 explicitly asserts the campaign on ledger state, rendered surfaces, and projections. Without intermediate outcome checks (e.g. after Wave 7: reconstructable scaffolding from typed events only; after Wave 12: reflection receipt present and next-stage proposal pending), criterion 9 is satisfied once at the end while intermediate greens remain plumbing-green. Add outcome assertions at each closed product loop, not only at the finale.
